intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Spend a full day hopping between the stunning Phi Phi islands by longtail boat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring hidden lagoons, and relaxing on pristine white-sand beaches. Includes snorkeling gear and a stop at Monkey Beach.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene with a guided evening walk through bustling night markets. Sample pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, som tum, and fresh coconut ice cream from local vendors. A true feast for the senses on a budget.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beach Kayaking & Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Rent a sea kayak and paddle along Koh Lanta's serene coastline, exploring sea caves and mangrove channels. End the day watching a breathtaking Andaman Sea sunset from Long Beach, one of Thailand's most peaceful and uncrowded stretches of sand.
experiences.location: Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao), Koh Lanta, Krabi

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Old City Temple & Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the ancient walled city of Chiang Mai on foot, visiting iconic temples like Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh. Afterward, graze through the famous Sunday Walking Street market sampling northern Thai specialties like khao soi, sai oua sausage, and fried insects.

experiences.name: Koh Samui Full Moon Beach Party & Coastal Bar Hop
experiences.description: Experience the legendary Thai beach party culture with an evening of live music, fire shows, and cocktails along the famous Haad Rin beach strip. Mingle with international travelers, enjoy neon-lit beach bars, and dance under the stars on one of Thailand's most iconic nightlife beaches.
experiences.location: Haad Rin Beach, Koh Phangan, Surat Thani

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport, clear customs, and take a budget minivan or shared shuttle to the nearest pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang Pier in Krabi). Board a ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Tonsai Village to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the beachfront walking street, watch fire shows on the beach, and soak in the island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during transit — grab a simple Thai rice dish or noodle soup from airport food courts (~150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick pad thai or fried rice from a street stall near the pier before boarding the ferry (~80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Dine at a local restaurant in Tonsai Village — try a green curry with rice or massaman curry (~150–200 THB). Wash it down with a fresh coconut (~50 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance during October as it can be busy. Carry some Thai Baht cash as ATMs on Phi Phi charge high fees. October is the tail end of rainy season — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike to Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–40 min uphill trek). The panoramic view of both Tonsai Bay and Loh Dalum Bay is stunning and completely free. Bring water and wear good shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Loh Dalum Beach for swimming and relaxing on the white sand. Rent a snorkel set from a local shop (~100–150 THB) and explore the clear waters just off the beach. Walk along the narrow island path connecting the two bays.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and browse the night market stalls. Enjoy the beach bar scene with cheap local beers and watch fire dancers perform on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh fruit smoothie and toast with egg from a small café near your guesthouse (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food stall near Loh Dalum Beach — mango sticky rice and a grilled skewer (~100 THB total)
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Thai restaurant in Tonsai Village — order a shared feast of tom yum soup, stir-fried morning glory, and jasmine rice (~200–250 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike is best done early morning before the heat kicks in. Stay hydrated. October weather may bring brief afternoon showers — keep a poncho handy.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling day trip departing from Tonsai Pier. These typically cover Maya Bay (made famous by 'The Beach'), Pileh Lagoon, Monkey Beach, and Bamboo Island. Book through a local tour operator the evening before (~800–1,200 THB including snorkel gear and lunch).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour visiting Bamboo Island's pristine white sand beach. Swim, snorkel, and relax. The boat typically returns to Phi Phi Don by 4–5 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the hotel, then head out for a sunset walk along Tonsai Bay. Grab a cheap Chang beer from a convenience store and sit on the beach to watch the colors fade.

meals.breakfast: Simple Thai breakfast at your guesthouse or nearby café — rice porridge (jok) with egg (~70–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in the boat tour — typically a simple Thai buffet on the beach or boat
meals.dinner: Try a local seafood BBQ stall near the pier — grilled fish with rice and papaya salad (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers — confirm with your tour operator that access is permitted. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Tipping the boat crew ~50–100 THB is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from the beach (~200–300 THB/hour) and paddle around the dramatic limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons near Phi Phi Don. Explore sea caves and small secluded coves at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat (~200–300 THB shared) to Phi Phi Leh's Pileh Lagoon for a peaceful swim in the emerald-green enclosed lagoon. Alternatively, walk to the quieter Viking Cave viewpoint area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cooking class or simply wander the village. Many guesthouses organize informal evening beach bonfires. Chat with fellow travelers and swap tips.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and coffee from a beachside vendor (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a 7-Eleven or local market before kayaking — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Dine at a cheap local Thai eatery away from the main tourist strip — look for plastic-chair restaurants with Thai menus for authentic and affordable food (~120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is best in the morning when seas are calmer. Wear a life jacket at all times. Bargain politely with longtail boat drivers for fair rates.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Islands to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hrs, ~300–400 THB). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town or Ao Nang area. Drop your bags and head to the Krabi Town Walking Street market if it's a weekend, or explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree views of Krabi's karst landscape. Entry is free. Allow 2–3 hours round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant night market (Maharaj Road Walking Street open Fri–Sun) or the riverside food stalls for an authentic local experience.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry at a Tonsai Village café — banana pancake and coffee (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Grab a local lunch in Krabi Town — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice) from a street stall (~60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Feast at the Krabi Town night market — pad see ew, grilled satay skewers, and fresh-squeezed juice (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — bring plenty of water and wear comfortable shoes. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) as it is a religious site. Monkeys near the temple can be cheeky with food.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget 4-island tour by longtail boat departing from Krabi Town or Ao Nang (~800–1,000 THB). Islands typically include Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor — famous for their sandbar connecting islands at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the 4-island tour — swim, snorkel, and explore the sandbar between Koh Tub and Koh Mor. The turquoise shallow water is perfect for wading. Return to Ao Nang by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Ao Nang Beach promenade. Browse the many street food carts and souvenir stalls. Enjoy a cheap cocktail or mocktail at a beachfront bar.

meals.breakfast: Simple guesthouse breakfast or nearby café — toast, eggs, and fruit (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch provided by the tour operator or bring your own snacks from a 7-Eleven
meals.dinner: Try a local Ao Nang restaurant — order a shared seafood platter with steamed rice (~200–300 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar between islands is only visible at low tide — check tide times with your tour operator. October can bring choppy seas; confirm the tour runs before booking. Book the night before for best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat to Railay Beach (~100–150 THB each way) — only accessible by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore East Railay and West Railay beaches, and visit the stunning Phra Nang Cave Beach with its sacred shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Railay Viewpoint trail (30–40 min, challenging but rewarding) for panoramic views of the peninsula. Alternatively, try rock climbing — Railay is world-famous for it, with beginner lessons available (~800–1,000 THB half-day).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from West Railay Beach — one of the most beautiful sunsets in Thailand. Take the longtail back to Ao Nang and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near your guesthouse before heading to the pier (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or buy from a small vendor on Railay Beach — prices are slightly higher here due to the remote location (~150–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Back in Ao Nang — eat at a local Thai restaurant off the main strip for better prices (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. Wear water shoes as the boat landing can be rocky. Keep valuables in a dry bag during the longtail ride.

day_by_day.morning: Take a minivan or bus from Krabi to Koh Lanta (~2.5 hrs, ~250–350 THB). Check in to a budget bungalow or guesthouse. Koh Lanta is known for its laid-back vibe and long sandy beaches. Settle in and explore Long Beach (Klong Dao Beach).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a motorbike (~200–300 THB/day) and explore the island. Drive south along the coast, stopping at Klong Nin Beach and Kantiang Bay — some of the most beautiful and less-crowded beaches on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Old Town (Ban Sala Dan or Lanta Old Town) on the east coast — a charming sea-gypsy village with wooden shophouses over the water. Browse local craft shops and watch the fishing boats come in.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Krabi or grab something at a roadside stall on the way (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Stop at a beachside restaurant on Klong Nin Beach — fresh fish and rice (~150–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Dine in Lanta Old Town — try a local family-run restaurant for authentic southern Thai cuisine with fresh seafood (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike rental requires a valid license. Drive carefully on Koh Lanta's roads, especially after rain. October may mean some beach restaurants are closed for low season — Old Town is a reliable option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Koh Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (~200 THB entry). Walk to the old lighthouse for sweeping ocean views and explore the mangrove boardwalk. Look for monitor lizards and tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Bamboo Bay or Waterfall Bay — secluded beaches within or near the national park. Swim, relax, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. These beaches are far less crowded than the north.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse area. Enjoy a relaxed evening with street food and a sunset drink at a beachfront bar on Long Beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café near Long Beach — fruit smoothie bowl or eggs on toast (~100–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the national park visit, or eat at the small park café (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Try a beachfront BBQ restaurant on Long Beach — grilled prawns, squid, and sticky rice (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Bring insect repellent for the mangrove walk. The southern tip roads can be rough — a motorbike with good tires is recommended. Carry enough cash as ATMs are limited in the south of the island.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget snorkeling day trip from Koh Lanta to the Trang Islands — including Koh Rok and Koh Ha, known for exceptional coral reefs and crystal-clear water (~1,200–1,500 THB including equipment and lunch). Depart early (~8 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling and island exploration. Koh Ha's underwater caves are a highlight — even non-divers can snorkel the entrance. The tour typically returns to Koh Lanta by 4–5 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and refresh. Enjoy a final evening on Koh Lanta — take a slow walk along the beach at sunset, grab a cheap Chang beer, and reflect on the journey so far.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your guesthouse before the tour departs (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in the day trip — typically a Thai lunch served on the beach
meals.dinner: Eat at a local night market stall or beachside restaurant — pad thai, spring rolls, and fresh coconut water (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trang Islands trip 1–2 days in advance. Koh Rok and Koh Ha are part of a marine national park — a park entry fee (~200 THB) may be added. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or speedboat from Koh Lanta to Koh Ngai or travel back toward Krabi/Phuket depending on onward plans. Alternatively, take a bus/minivan north toward Phuket (~3–4 hrs, ~350–450 THB). Check in to a budget hostel or guesthouse in Phuket Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized area of Sino-Portuguese shophouses, colorful street art, and hip cafés. Walk along Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Romanee. Entry is free — this is a walking exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the famous Sunday Night Market (Lard Yai) if it's a Sunday, or the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) on weekends. Otherwise, explore the local bars and street food scene in Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab something at the pier — roti with banana and condensed milk (~50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat at a local kopitiam (Chinese-Thai coffee shop) in Phuket Old Town — try Hokkien noodles or dim sum (~80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food in Phuket Old Town — try o-tao (oyster omelette), moo hong (braised pork), and khanom jeen (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes. Many historic buildings are being restored; explore side streets for hidden gems. Tuk-tuks in Phuket are notoriously expensive — negotiate firmly or use Grab app.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or songthaew (~30–50 THB) to Kata Beach or Karon Beach — less touristy and more affordable than Patong. Spend the morning swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the long stretch of sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Promthep Cape for stunning coastal views at the southern tip of Phuket. Then head to Chalong Temple (Wat Chalong) — Phuket's most important Buddhist temple and completely free to enter. Dress modestly.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Patong's Bangla Road for a taste of Phuket's famous nightlife — even on a budget, it's worth experiencing the energy. Grab cheap street food and drinks from vendors rather than bars to keep costs low.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café in Phuket Town (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall at Kata or Karon Beach — fried rice or noodle soup (~100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food on Bangla Road or nearby side streets — satay, grilled corn, fresh fruit shakes, and pad thai (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Avoid renting a motorbike in Phuket if unfamiliar with Thai traffic — it's heavier and more chaotic than the islands. Use songthaews (shared red trucks) for cheap local transport. Keep bags close in Patong at night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite spot or explore somewhere new. If time allows, visit Big Buddha (Phuket's giant marble Buddha statue on a hilltop) for free panoramic views and a peaceful atmosphere. Dress respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to your guesthouse, pack up, and check out. Make your way to Phuket International Airport via shared minivan or airport bus (~100–150 THB). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Phuket. Reflect on an incredible 13-day budget adventure through Thailand's most beautiful islands and beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — jok (rice porridge) with pork and ginger, or khao tom at a local café (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at the airport food court or a final street food snack before heading to the airport (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Buy any last-minute souvenirs in Phuket Old Town or at the night market — prices are far cheaper than the airport. Stock up on Thai snacks (dried mango, coconut chips, chili paste) at a local supermarket before flying. Budget tip: use the Grab app throughout Thailand for fair-priced taxis and food delivery.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and take a pre-arranged shuttle or taxi to Rassada Pier in Phuket or Krabi town. Board a high-speed ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Tonsai Village beachfront to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the colorful street food stalls along the main walking street. Watch the sunset from the beachside bars with a refreshing cocktail in hand.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a Thai-style rice porridge (Jok) or a sandwich at the terminal.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at Krabi or Phuket pier area — try a local noodle shop for Pad See Ew or a bowl of boat noodles (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food stalls — grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh spring rolls. Try a local restaurant like Papaya Restaurant for affordable Thai classics (~300–450 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry tickets in advance during October as it is shoulder season and boats may have limited seats. Bring baht cash for the ferry and small vendors on Phi Phi. Keep luggage manageable as porters on Phi Phi carry bags by hand or cart.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 minute uphill trek). The panoramic view of the twin bays of Phi Phi Don is breathtaking and best enjoyed in the cooler morning hours. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh island. Visit the iconic Maya Bay (check current access regulations as it has limited daily visitor quotas), snorkel at Pileh Lagoon, and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs of Viking Cave.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and enjoy a relaxing beachside dinner. Watch fire dancers perform on the beach — a signature Phi Phi evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Boutique hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try Thai-style toast with pandan jam and a Thai iced tea (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the boat tour or grab lunch at a beachside shack on Phi Phi Leh — fresh coconut and fruit skewers.
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant in Tonsai — try Unni's Restaurant for a mix of Thai and Western dishes. Grilled fish with garlic and pepper is highly recommended (~400–600 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor limits and may require timed entry. Confirm with your tour operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a rash guard, and an underwater camera for snorkeling. October weather may bring occasional afternoon showers — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a guided kayaking tour from Tonsai Bay. Paddle through the calm turquoise waters around Phi Phi Don, exploring hidden coves, sea caves, and quiet beaches like Loh Dalum Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Loh Dalum Beach — one of Phi Phi's most beautiful stretches of sand. Swim, sunbathe, or try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP boards available for rent on the beach). Explore the small boutique shops and local art galleries in Tonsai Village.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset cruise around Phi Phi Island — many operators offer 2-hour sunset boat trips with snorkeling stops and onboard drinks. A perfect way to end the day.

meals.breakfast: Local market near Tonsai pier — fresh tropical fruit plate, roti with banana and honey, and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Beachside café on Loh Dalum Bay — green papaya salad (Som Tum), grilled corn, and a cold Chang beer (~250–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Return to Tonsai Village and dine at a mid-range Thai restaurant — try Garlic Restaurant for their famous garlic and pepper dishes with jasmine rice (~350–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals typically cost 150–300 THB per hour. Sunset cruises cost approximately 600–900 THB per person and should be booked in the afternoon from pier operators. October evenings can be warm and humid — dress lightly.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning longtail boat to the quieter Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai), located about 30 minutes north of Phi Phi Don. Enjoy pristine white sand beaches, crystal-clear water, and excellent snorkeling with minimal crowds in the morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for more snorkeling among vibrant coral reefs. Return to Phi Phi Don by mid-afternoon and explore the less-visited eastern side of the island near Loh Bakao Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cooking class in Tonsai Village — many local operators offer 2–3 hour evening Thai cooking sessions where you learn to make Pad Thai, Tom Yum soup, and green curry from scratch.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a local bakery — banana pancakes and coffee are a Phi Phi classic (~100 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or eat at a small beach shack on Bamboo Island — fresh grilled fish and sticky rice (~200–300 THB).
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you cooked in your cooking class — most classes include a full meal of everything prepared. Supplement with a light dessert from a street stall (~50–100 THB for mango sticky rice).

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boat charters to Bamboo Island cost approximately 1,500–2,000 THB per boat (shareable with other travelers). Cooking classes typically cost 900–1,500 THB per person and should be booked a day in advance. Bring insect repellent for the evening class.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Phi Phi boutique stay and take the morning ferry to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel near Krabi Town or Ao Nang Beach. Drop your bags and head to the famous Krabi Town Walking Street (if it's a weekend) or explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking 360-degree view over Krabi's limestone karsts and jungle landscape. The climb takes about 45 minutes each way and is rewarding but challenging.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant night market (Maharaj Road Walking Street on weekends or the daily Chao Fa Night Market). Sample an array of street food and local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Tonsai before ferry departure — toast, eggs, and Thai iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant — try Ruen Mai Restaurant for authentic Southern Thai cuisine. Massaman curry with roti is a must (~200–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market — grilled seafood on skewers, pad kra pao (basil stir fry), coconut ice cream, and fresh fruit shakes (~200–300 THB for a full spread).

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is not recommended in the midday heat — aim to start by 3:00–4:00 PM to enjoy the sunset from the top. Bring plenty of water and wear non-slip shoes. The temple is free to enter but modest dress is required.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day Four Islands tour departing from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier. Visit Koh Poda (stunning white sand beach), Koh Gai (Chicken Island with excellent snorkeling), Tup Island (connected by a sandbar at low tide), and Koh Mor. Snorkel, swim, and relax across all four islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour — the sandbar connecting Tup Island and Koh Mor is a highlight. Wade through shallow turquoise water between the two islands. Return to Ao Nang by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Ao Nang Beach promenade. Browse souvenir shops, try street food snacks, and enjoy a beachside drink as the sun sets over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Ao Nang — Thai omelette over rice (Khao Khai Dao) and fresh orange juice (~120–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch included on most Four Islands tours — typically a simple Thai buffet served on one of the islands or on the boat.
meals.dinner: Ao Nang beachfront restaurant — try Last Fisherman Bar for fresh grilled seafood platters with a view of the illuminated karst cliffs (~500–700 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Four Islands tours cost approximately 600–900 THB per person and depart around 8:30–9:00 AM. Book through your hotel or a reputable local tour operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15-minute ride, not accessible by road due to surrounding cliffs). Explore East Railay and West Railay beaches. Hike the short jungle trail to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of the most beautiful beaches in Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try rock climbing on Railay's famous limestone karst walls — Railay is one of Southeast Asia's top rock climbing destinations. Beginner half-day courses are available from local operators on the beach. Alternatively, kayak around the dramatic cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from West Railay Beach before taking the longtail boat back to Ao Nang. Enjoy a quiet evening dinner and rest after an active day.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang café — fresh fruit smoothie bowl and granola (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Railay Beach restaurant — Tom Kha Gai (coconut chicken soup) and steamed rice at a beachside eatery (~300–400 THB).
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food area — Pad Thai from a wok stall, fresh spring rolls, and Thai iced tea (~200–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay cost approximately 100–150 THB per person each way. Rock climbing half-day beginner courses cost around 800–1,200 THB per person including gear and instruction. Railay has no ATMs — bring sufficient cash. October may bring brief afternoon rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan-ferry combination (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Check into a mid-range beachfront bungalow or guesthouse on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach. Settle in and take a morning walk along the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses built on stilts over the sea. Browse local crafts, visit the small community museum, and chat with friendly locals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your beach area and enjoy a relaxed sunset dinner. Koh Lanta is known for its laid-back atmosphere and beautiful sunsets over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Krabi hotel before departure — or grab something at the pier.
meals.lunch: Old Town Koh Lanta — fresh seafood lunch at a stilted wooden restaurant overlooking the sea. Try steamed fish with lime and garlic (~350–500 THB).
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — grilled prawns, papaya salad, and sticky rice with a sunset view (~400–600 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Koh Lanta run seasonally — confirm schedules in advance as October is shoulder season. Scooter rentals on Koh Lanta cost approximately 200–300 THB per day. Old Town is best visited in the late afternoon when the light is golden and the heat has eased.

day_by_day.morning: Join a snorkeling day trip to the Koh Lanta Marine National Park islands — including Koh Rok Nok, Koh Rok Nai, and Koh Ha. These remote islands offer some of the best snorkeling and diving in the Andaman Sea with pristine coral gardens and diverse marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Ha's underwater caverns and dramatic limestone formations. Relax on the white sand beach of Koh Rok Nok — one of the most remote and beautiful beaches in southern Thailand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Visit the local evening market near Saladan Pier for fresh seafood and Thai street food. Enjoy a relaxed evening by the beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — Thai-style fried rice with egg and fresh fruit (~150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch provided on the snorkeling day trip — typically a simple Thai meal served on the boat or beach.
meals.dinner: Saladan Pier area seafood market — pick your fresh catch and have it grilled to order with your choice of sauce (~400–600 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling day trips to the Marine National Park cost approximately 1,200–1,800 THB per person including park fees, equipment, and lunch. Book through your guesthouse or a local dive shop. Koh Rok and Koh Ha are protected areas — do not touch or stand on coral.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Koh Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island. Walk the jungle trail to a scenic viewpoint and visit the lighthouse. Keep an eye out for monitor lizards, hornbills, and other wildlife in the lush forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Bamboo Bay (Ao Mai Phai) within the national park — a secluded beach accessible by a short jungle walk. Swim in the calm, clear water. In the mid-afternoon, head back to your beach and enjoy a spa treatment at one of Koh Lanta's affordable beachside massage parlors.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your last evening on Koh Lanta with a beachfire dinner experience. Many restaurants along Long Beach and Klong Nin offer tables right on the sand with lanterns and candlelight.

meals.breakfast: Beachside café — banana pancakes, fresh coconut, and coffee (~120–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Picnic at Bamboo Bay or a snack from the national park entrance area — fresh coconut water and fruit (~100 THB).
meals.dinner: Klong Nin Beach restaurant — try Time for Lime (a social enterprise restaurant and cooking school) for elevated Thai cuisine in a beautiful setting (~500–700 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta National Park entrance fee is approximately 200 THB for foreigners. A traditional Thai massage on the beach costs 250–400 THB per hour. Time for Lime restaurant is popular — make a reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Koh Lanta accommodation and take the ferry or minivan back to Krabi. Connect onward to Phuket by shared minivan or bus (approximately 3–4 hours total travel). Check into a mid-range hotel in Phuket Old Town or Patong Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized heritage area with beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture. Walk along Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee, admire the colorful street art, and visit the Chinpracha House museum.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the famous Phuket Sunday Walking Street (if it's a Sunday) or the Chillva Market / Naka Weekend Market for an incredible spread of street food, local crafts, and live music. A quintessential Phuket evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Koh Lanta before departure — simple guesthouse fare or a local coffee shop.
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town — try Kopitiam by Wilai for authentic Phuket-style cuisine. The Mee Hokkien (Hokkien noodles) and Por Pia (spring rolls) are legendary (~250–400 THB).
meals.dinner: Phuket Walking Street or Naka Market — an adventurous spread of oyster omelettes, grilled meats, Phuket-style satay, and fresh fruit juices (~250–400 THB for a full street food dinner).

day_by_day.notes: The Phuket Sunday Walking Street runs every Sunday evening from 4:00 PM to 10:00 PM on Thalang Road in Old Town. Naka Weekend Market operates on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings. Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — one of Thailand's most iconic landscapes. Join a group tour by speedboat or traditional longtail boat. Visit James Bond Island (Koh Tapu), the sea caves of Koh Phing Kan, and kayak through the eerie mangrove tunnels and hongs (inland lagoons).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour — explore the floating Muslim fishing village of Koh Panyee, built entirely on stilts over the water. Browse the village's souvenir shops and enjoy the unique cultural experience. Return to Phuket by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Patong Beach for your final big evening out. Watch the vibrant Bangla Road night scene, enjoy a rooftop bar cocktail, or catch a Thai boxing (Muay Thai) match at Patong Boxing Stadium.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Old Town — Dim Sum and Chinese tea in the Sino-Portuguese tradition (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koh Panyee floating village — fresh seafood curry and rice with a view over Phang Nga Bay (~300–450 THB).
meals.dinner: Patong Beach area — try Baan Rim Pa for upscale Thai dining on a cliff overlooking the Andaman Sea, or opt for a more casual beachfront restaurant (~500–800 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours cost approximately 1,200–2,000 THB per person depending on the operator and boat type. Book through your hotel the evening before. Muay Thai tickets at Patong Boxing Stadium cost approximately 1,500–2,000 THB for ringside seats. Book in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Phuket. Visit Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a last swim in the Andaman Sea — both are calmer and less crowded than Patong. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the Phuket Weekend Market (Naka Market) or local shops in Old Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final Thai lunch and begin making your way to Phuket International Airport. Allow at least 1.5–2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 13 days of beaches, islands, and street food across southern Thailand.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — Jok (rice porridge) with ginger and a soft-boiled egg, or Khanom Jeen (rice noodles with curry) at a local morning market (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town farewell lunch — return to a favorite spot or try Phuket-style yellow crab curry (Gaeng Poo) at a local restaurant (~300–500 THB).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a light meal before departure — Phuket Airport has several decent restaurant options for a final taste of Thai food.

day_by_day.notes: Pack any liquid souvenirs (fish sauce, curry pastes, chili oils) in checked luggage to comply with airline carry-on restrictions. Exchange remaining Thai Baht at the airport or save for future travels. Consider leaving a review for your favorite experiences to help other travelers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Arrange a pre-booked private transfer to the pier, then board a private speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Enjoy the scenic 1.5-hour Andaman Sea crossing with welcome drinks on board. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind on your private terrace and take a refreshing dip in the resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle stroll along Tonsai Bay waterfront to acclimate to the island atmosphere. Watch the sunset from a clifftop viewpoint above the village.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Light snack box provided on the private speedboat transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved fine-casual spot known for fresh seafood, Thai curries and wood-fired dishes; reserve a candlelit table overlooking the bay

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private speedboat transfer and resort check-in in advance. October falls in the shoulder-to-wet season; sea conditions are generally fine but carry a light rain jacket. Confirm resort early check-in availability.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort. Follow with a hearty breakfast before embarking on a guided snorkeling excursion to Shark Point and Anemone Reef — two of the Andaman's most vibrant coral gardens, teeming with leopard sharks, turtles and reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh island. Visit the iconic Maya Bay (book a timed entry permit in advance), explore the emerald lagoon of Pileh Cove and swim through the natural arch at Viking Cave. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch served on the boat by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a sunset cocktail at the clifftop bar. Dine under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict and fresh-pressed juices at the resort's beachfront restaurant
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic box on the private boat — poached prawns, papaya salad, artisan sandwiches and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: The Phi Phi Natural Resort's signature seafood BBQ — choose your catch from the day's market and have it grilled with herb butters and Thai spices

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor caps; book timed-entry permits weeks in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and an underwater camera. Snorkeling equipment is provided by the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to Phi Phi Viewpoint 3 — the highest vantage point on the island — for a breathtaking panorama of the twin bays and the entire Phi Phi archipelago. Depart early to beat the heat. A private guide will lead you through jungle trails and share the island's ecological history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking adventure through the hidden sea caves and mangrove channels on the quieter eastern shore of Koh Phi Phi Don. Discover secluded beaches accessible only by water. Return to the resort for a private Thai massage and spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tonsai Village night market for authentic street food — a curated, premium street food walk with a local food guide who navigates the best stalls.

meals.breakfast: Almond croissants, tropical smoothie bowls and specialty Thai coffee at the resort café
meals.lunch: Beachside dining at Ciao Bella — fresh seafood pasta, grilled calamari and chilled Aperol Spritz with Andaman views
meals.dinner: Premium street food tour: pad see ew, crispy oyster omelette (hoy tod), mango sticky rice and fresh coconut ice cream from Tonsai Village's finest vendors

day_by_day.notes: Start the viewpoint hike no later than 07:30 to avoid midday heat. The street food walk is best experienced with a knowledgeable guide who can identify the top vendors and explain each dish.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island-hopping adventure by private speedboat. First stop: Koh Yung (Mosquito Island) — a pristine, rarely visited island with crystal-clear waters and a deserted white sand beach. Snorkel the untouched reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Phai (Bamboo Island) — known for its powdery white beach and shallow turquoise lagoon. Swim, sunbathe and enjoy a freshly prepared Thai lunch served on the beach by your private crew. Afternoon stop at Koh Bida Nok for world-class drift snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don for a private sunset dinner on the beach — a resort-arranged table-for-two on the sand with a bespoke Thai tasting menu, lanterns and live acoustic guitar.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai-Western buffet breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Private beach lunch on Bamboo Island: grilled barracuda, green papaya salad, jasmine rice and fresh pineapple
meals.dinner: Private beachfront tasting menu — tom kha goong, massaman lamb, pandan-infused sea bass and lychee sorbet with champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a highlight day — confirm the private speedboat and beach dinner setup at least 48 hours in advance. Bring extra reef-safe sunscreen and a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat transfer to Krabi Town. Check in to a luxury property such as Rayavadee Resort in Railay Beach or Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Krabi. Morning at leisure to settle in and explore the resort grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic Railay Beach peninsula — accessible only by boat. Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach, one of Thailand's most spectacular stretches of sand framed by towering limestone karsts. Kayak through the hidden lagoon inside the karst interior.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar. Dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Phi Phi resort before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at Railay Beach Terrace — grilled tiger prawns, som tum and cold Singha beer with karst views
meals.dinner: Rayavadee's Grotto Restaurant — carved inside a natural cave, serving elevated Thai cuisine with an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Phi Phi to Railay takes approximately 2 hours by speedboat. Railay is car-free — all movement is on foot or by longtail boat. Book Grotto Restaurant well in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Rock climbing lesson on the iconic limestone karsts of Railay with a certified UIAA guide — suitable for beginners and intermediate climbers. The karsts offer over 200 routes with unparalleled Andaman Sea views from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Four Islands Tour by private longtail: visit Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub and Koh Mor — a chain of small islands connected by a sandbar at low tide. Snorkel, swim and photograph the surreal sandbar formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for a premium street food and night market experience at Maharaj Road Walking Street with a private food guide.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit, congee and Thai iced coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the sandbar between Koh Tub and Koh Mor — prepared by your private boat crew
meals.dinner: Krabi Town night market: crab fried rice (khao pad puu), satay skewers, fresh spring rolls and roti with condensed milk; end with a craft cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Krabi River

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar between Koh Tub and Koh Mor is only visible at low tide — plan the boat tour timing accordingly. Rock climbing helmets and harnesses are provided; wear closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a 360-degree panorama of Krabi's limestone karst landscape and paddy fields. Arrive before 08:00 for the best light and cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through the mangrove forests of Ao Thalane Bay — a UNESCO-recognized wetland ecosystem. Paddle through cathedral-like mangrove tunnels and spot monitor lizards, kingfishers and mudskippers with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise along the Krabi River estuary on a traditional converted rice barge — champagne, canapés and a live classical Thai music performance.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh-baked pastries and Thai iced tea from a local bakery near Tiger Cave Temple
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at Krabi Organic Farm Restaurant — locally grown vegetables, free-range chicken in red curry and fresh herb salads
meals.dinner: Four-course dinner on the sunset river cruise — tom yum goong, beef massaman, steamed sea bass with lime and chili, and black sticky rice with coconut cream

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for Tiger Cave Temple (cover shoulders and knees). The mangrove kayak tour operates best at high tide — confirm timing with your guide. Book the river cruise dinner at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Ao Nang for a speedboat departure to Koh Lanta — a larger, more laid-back island south of Krabi. Check in to a luxury resort such as Pimalai Resort & Spa or Layana Resort. Morning at leisure to explore the resort's beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town — a charming 19th-century Chinese-Malay fishing village built on stilts over the sea. Browse antique shops, art galleries and spice traders. Visit the old Lanta lighthouse at the southern tip of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside dinner at one of Koh Lanta's acclaimed restaurants as the sun dips behind Koh Rok on the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Krabi resort before departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a local restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — whole steamed fish with ginger, stir-fried morning glory and jasmine rice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pimalai's Bulow Terrace — contemporary Thai cuisine with an extensive wine cellar, overlooking Ba Kan Tiang Bay

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat from Ao Nang to Koh Lanta takes approximately 1.5 hours. Koh Lanta Old Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle — rent one from your resort. October seas are generally calm but confirm conditions on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise snorkeling expedition to Koh Rok Nok and Koh Rok Nai — two of Thailand's most pristine marine national park islands, accessible only by speedboat from Koh Lanta. The reefs here are among the healthiest in the Andaman and are home to whale sharks (seasonal).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Koh Lanta for a private Thai cooking class at a local chef's home — learn to make green curry paste from scratch, pad thai with fresh river prawns and mango sticky rice. Enjoy your creations as lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach. Explore the Saladan Pier night market for local street food.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before the snorkeling departure
meals.lunch: Your own Thai cooking class creations — green curry, pad thai and mango sticky rice
meals.dinner: Saladan Pier night market: grilled corn, fresh oysters, coconut pancakes (khanom bueang) and freshly squeezed sugarcane juice; followed by a premium seafood dinner at a local restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a national park — entry fees apply. Arrive early to enjoy the reefs before day-trip boats from Krabi arrive. The cooking class should be booked in advance and runs approximately 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private boat charter around the Koh Lanta Marine National Park — visiting Koh Ha (Five Islands), a world-renowned dive site with underwater caverns, swim-throughs and dramatic topography. Snorkeling or introductory diving available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Ngai (Hai) — a serene, largely undeveloped island with a long beach of powdery white sand. Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise waters and relax on the beach with a cocktail from the boat's cooler.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta for a private in-villa dinner arranged by the resort — a personal chef prepares a 5-course Thai feast in your villa with wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit, yogurt and granola at the resort
meals.lunch: Freshly prepared lunch on the boat — grilled fish, rice, salads and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Private in-villa 5-course dinner: amuse-bouche of betel leaf with toasted coconut, tom kha soup, green mango salad, grilled lobster with tamarind glaze, and pandan crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ha is a premier dive site — if interested in scuba, arrange a PADI-certified dive guide through the resort. The in-villa dinner requires 48-hour advance notice. Bring an underwater torch for the cave snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wellness ritual at the resort spa — traditional Thai herbal compress massage followed by a Hammam steam and an Andaman sea-salt body scrub. Followed by a slow breakfast on your villa terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta National Park on the southern tip of the island — jungle trails through old-growth forest to secluded beaches. Spot dusky langur monkeys, hornbills and sea eagles with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Krabi Airport or pier for onward travel to Phuket. Check in to a luxury property in Phuket — such as Amanpuri, Trisara or Keemala Resort in the Kamala/Surin area.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely villa terrace breakfast — eggs your way, fresh juice, pastries and Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Koh Lanta National Park — prepared by the resort: baguette sandwiches, fruit and homemade lemonade
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Phuket resort — Trisara's PRU Restaurant (one Michelin star) for a farm-and-sea-to-table tasting menu using hyper-local ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Depart Koh Lanta by speedboat or vehicle ferry to Krabi, then transfer to Phuket (approximately 3 hours total). Book Trisara PRU Restaurant well in advance — it is one of Thailand's most acclaimed dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Phuket's historic Old Town — a UNESCO-listed enclave of Sino-Portuguese shophouses, colonial-era mansions and vibrant street art. Join a private heritage walking tour with an architectural historian. Visit Wat Chalong, the island's most revered Buddhist temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Surin Beach or Bang Tao Beach — two of Phuket's most upscale stretches of sand. Lounge at a premium beach club such as Catch Beach Club or Twinpalms' On the Rocks for the afternoon. Jet ski, paddleboard or simply relax with a cocktail in hand.
day_by_day.evening: Phuket's premium street food scene: join a curated night food tour through the Old Town's Sunday Walking Street or Malin Plaza — sampling the island's best local dishes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, dim sum and specialty Phuket coffee (kopi)
meals.lunch: Catch Beach Club — Mediterranean-Thai fusion, grilled seafood platters and frozen cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Old Town street food tour: Phuket-style hokkien noodles (mee sua), crab yellow curry (pu pad pong karee), oh tao (oyster and taro pancake) and fresh-pressed sugarcane juice; finish with a nightcap at a rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Sunday Walking Street operates weekly; check the day's market schedule. Surin Beach has strong currents in October — swim between the flags.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — sunrise beach walk at Nai Harn Beach, one of Phuket's most beautiful and least commercialized bays. Followed by a farewell Thai massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping at Central Festival Phuket or the boutiques of Boat Avenue in Cherng Talay — pick up premium Thai silk, artisan ceramics, bespoke jewelry and high-quality spice kits. Enjoy a final Thai lunch before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days across Thailand's finest islands.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full Thai and Western spread, fresh juices, pastries and champagne
meals.lunch: Final Thai lunch at Suay Restaurant, Phuket Old Town — celebrated for its elevated Southern Thai cuisine using heirloom recipes and premium local ingredients
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for airport check-in and security. Arrange your private airport transfer the evening before. Declare any food items or cultural artifacts at customs. Pack Thai condiments and snacks in checked luggage.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
